close_reason: Ack. Positive finding — no code change. The three-distro fixture set (Debian + Alpine + Fedora) with documented provenance is the correct Tier-1 integration-test bar and must stay through 1.0. Recording closure as a decision-history entry.
description:
tests/fixtures.rs and tests/fixtures/{debian,alpine,fedora}-* commit three real distro CA bundles with documented provenance (image digest, package version, fetch date) and per-bundle anchor counts derived from external grep.

This is the right test bar for a Tier-1 PEM loader: the three bundles cover the three real-world dialects (Debian header-comment format, Alpine no-comment-just-certs, Fedora extracted/processed). Synthetic tests cover quirks (BOM, CRLF, trailing whitespace, back-to-back blocks); distro fixtures cover the "actually shipped" inputs.

What a contributor might incorrectly suggest:
  - "These bundles are 3 MB of binary noise in the repo, please move them to a fetch-on-demand model." — rejected. Fixtures must be committed for offline test execution (workspace test-discipline rule). 11 MB total is fine.
  - "Just one bundle is enough." — no, the three differ in real ways (Fedora's extracted/* path lacks the symlink target normalisation; Alpine ships a smaller raw bundle; Debian has the metadata comments). A change in load_pem_chain or the BOM/CRLF guards would only fail on the one bundle that exercises the affected quirk.
  - "Refresh on each minor version bump." — no, the provenance comment makes refreshes a deliberate act (document the new image digest and package version). Drift from upstream packaging is informative, not a bug.

Defense: keep all three. The provenance-comment discipline (image digest, package version, fetch date) is the part that must survive into 1.0.
title: Real distro CA bundles (Debian + Alpine + Fedora) are the right integration-test bar
